children: The market for French government bonds, or OATs, will have to navigate the twists and turns of the electoral campaign, which could elicit further spread volatility, says MFS Investment Management's Peter Goves in a note. MFS IM, however, does not envisage stress that would compromise the primary market, the head of developed market debt sovereign research says. "France will be able to fund itself, the question will be at what interest rate," he says. While yield spreads have widened, "they are not (yet) adversely affecting affordability metrics significantly," he says. MFS IM's base case sees volatility until electoral certainty can be achieved--and with it, credibility on restoring fiscal rectitude. The 10-year French OAT-German Bund yield spread last trades at 155 basis points, according to LSEG. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
